title: Text Sanitizer Pipeline
description: Build a pipeline that cleans a text file: convert to lowercase, remove punctuation, and count word frequency.
problemStatement:
Write a script `word_freq.sh` that processes a text file and prints the most common words. It should:

1. Accept the text file as an argument (validate).
2. Convert all letters to lowercase using `tr`.
3. Replace all punctuation characters (.,!?;:) with spaces using `tr`.
4. Squeeze multiple spaces into one using `tr -s`.
5. Convert spaces to newlines so each word is on its own line (`tr ' ' '\n'`).
6. Sort, count with `uniq -c`, sort numerically descending.
7. Display the top 20 words.
8. Ignore empty lines.

Test with a sample paragraph.
hints: Use `grep -v '^$'` to remove empty lines before the final sort.
Ensure you handle contractions/apostrophes appropriately (maybe delete them).
solutionCode:
#!/bin/bash
# word_freq.sh – word frequency counter

file="$1"
if [ ! -f "$file" ]; then
  echo "Error: file not found" >&2
  exit 1
fi

cat "$file" | tr 'A-Z' 'a-z' | tr -d '[:punct:]' | tr -s ' ' '\n' | grep -v '^$' | sort | uniq -c | sort -nr | head -n 20
